liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **The Other One** (2 reviews): Reviewer singles out The Other One as especially deserving of praise; Reviewer highlights a nice Other One, agreeing with an earlier reviewer [5][6]
- **Jack Straw** (1 other source): Jack Straw is missing from Deadlists but appears in Deadbase and on the official digital Download Series release of the full show [1]
- **Beat it on Down the Line** (1 review): Two large dropouts affect this song on the Archive version, likely why it's omitted from Download Series Vol. 3 [9]

## Setlist highlights

- **WCMF announcer**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [12]
- **see y'all later, crowd**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [12]

## The recordings

- **gd1971-10-26.176458.wcmf-fm.flac1644** (recommended): FM broadcast; 24 songs; 176 min; rated 4/5 by 1 [1]. Said about its sound: FM broadcast has dropouts but fuller sound, with more bass and piano, according to the reviewer [11]
- **gd71-10-26.sbd.cotsman.9761.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 162 min; rated 4/5 by 8 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer finds the soundboard's sound quality poor [3]

## Around the show

- Reviewer's father attended college at the Rochester campus where the Dead played [3]
- Reviewer attended on their 21st birthday and saw Jerry play pedal steel with the New Riders [4]
- Show features Keith Godchaux on keyboards and Billy K. on drums [5]
- The University of Rochester gym held about 2000 people, making this a small campus show [8]
- The album Skull Fuck was shipping that week, so the audience likely hadn't heard many songs [8]
- Reviewer prefers this FM broadcast to the Download Series Vol. 3 board, which sounds generic and sterile [11]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1971-10-26.176458.wcmf-fm.flac1644**: taped by dubbed by David Bernis; transferred by Doug Rice for expert transfer from Beta, Andrew F; source: WCMF-FM > Reels > ? > Beta HiFi. [1]. Also: Source is the WCMF Rochester FM broadcast, described as an antique historical item [1]
- **gd71-10-26.sbd.cotsman.9761.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [2]. Also: Though broadcast on radio, the show apparently never circulated among traders and was only a DeadBase entry until the archive era; The Archive version appears to derive from cotsman's soundboard; Discs 1 and 2 come from one source, while disc 3 comes from a second [2][8][9]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Grateful Dead & NRPS, The Palestra, U. of Rochester, Poster](https://www.dead.net/archives/1971/artwork/grateful-dead-nrps-palestra-u-rochester-poster) [13]
